<reason>A wins by distinguishing meaningful access obligations from categorically disregarding reputational costs. Its boutique challenge exposed B’s narrowing of a motion without a dominance exception, while its substantial-loss threshold made the competing interests concrete. B compellingly explained creators’ dependence on chokepoints, but did not adequately justify unlimited commercial exposure. Its closing also mischaracterized A’s substantive safeguards as mere paperwork. B’s sweeping claims about selective exclusions and documented harms received less weight because their grounding was not established.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A answered the “zero enforceable duties” challenge with independent review empowered to restore access, evidence of substantial expected losses, and consideration of less restrictive measures. This materially defeated B’s unchecked-gatekeeper framing; B’s subsequent “ban with paperwork” response did not engage the actual threshold.</best_rebuttal>
